messages.subject: mediation controlling for common method factor
parts:
Dear list,

I am trying to fit a mediation model, controlling for common method factor and some demographic variables. So essentially, it is a bifactor model. Many of the standard errors were not estimated in the model, but lavaan did not show me any error or warning, could you please give me some advice? Please see the code and the results below. Thank you very much.

Best regards,


ya



> model='
+ el =~ NA*youdaoel + lijieel + yuanzhuel; youdaoel ~~ 1*youdaoel;
+ thriv =~ NA*vatalityth + equal("thriv=~vatalityth")*learningth; thriv ~~ 1*thriv;
+ creat =~ NA*generationcr + promotioncr + realizationcr; creat ~~ 1*creat;
+ common =~ NA*youdaoel + lijieel + yuanzhuel + vatalityth + learningth + generationcr + promotioncr + realizationcr;
+ common ~~ 1*common;
+
+ # controlling for demographic covariates:
+ gender =~ sex; sex ~~ 0*sex;
+ old =~ age; age ~~ 0*age;
+ edu =~ degree; degree ~~ 0*degree;
+ time1 =~ work1; work1 ~~ 0*work1;
+ time3 =~ work3; work3 ~~ 0*work3;
+ creat + thriv + el ~ gender + old + edu + time1 + time3
+
+ common ~~ 0*el; common ~~ 0*thriv; common ~~ 0*creat;
+ common ~~ 0*gender; common ~~ 0*old; common ~~ 0*edu; common ~~ 0*time1; common ~~ 0*time3;
+
+ thriv ~ a*el
+ creat ~ b*thriv + cdash*el
+ ab:= a*b; total:= a*b + cdash; portion:= ab/total
+ '

messages.subject: Re: mediation controlling for common method factor
parts:
Dear list,

I have located the problem. It was a careless mistake, for the latent variable “el”, I should fix the latent variance instead of the variance of the “youdaoel”. Sorry for the trouble.

However, after correcting the mistake, the output still looks problematic. I realize that this becomes actually a SEM question rather than a lavaan question, but could you share me some experience on handling this kind of model please? Specifically, although the model fit looks ok, the loadings for some indicators are questionably low, and the portion of the mediation effect I define to calculate was higher than 1, not mention the result of the new defined indirect effect a*b =  251.868. 

Most of the examples of the bifactor model I saw use CFA as their base. I am employing the bifactor model to control for the common method factor in a full SEM model. Do you aware of any example close to my case? 

Please see the new details below. Thank you very much.

Best regards,


ya



> model='
+ el =~ NA*youdaoel + lijieel + yuanzhuel; el ~~ 1*el;

+ thriv =~ NA*vatalityth + equal("thriv=~vatalityth")*learningth; thriv ~~ 1*thriv;
+ creat =~ NA*generationcr + promotioncr + realizationcr; creat ~~ 1*creat;
+ common =~ NA*youdaoel + lijieel + yuanzhuel + vatalityth + learningth + generationcr + promotioncr + realizationcr; 
+ common ~~ 1*common;
+ 
+ # controlling for demographic covariates:
+ gender =~ sex; sex ~~ 0*sex;

+ time1 =~ work1; work1 ~~ 0*work1;
+ time3 =~ work3; work3 ~~ 0*work3;

+

messages.subject: Re: mediation controlling for common method factor
parts:
On 07/02/2016 03:24 AM, xinxi813 wrote:
> However, after correcting the mistake, the output still looks
> problematic. I realize that this becomes actually a SEM question rather
> than a lavaan question, but could you share me some experience on
> handling this kind of model please? Specifically, although the model fit
> looks ok, the loadings for some indicators are questionably low

The problem with these 'common' factors is that we really have no idea
what they capture. Even worse, we do not know what the specific factors
capture, after we have 'controlled for' the common factor. So
interpretations is always difficult. Anyways, SEMNET is a better source
for opinions about this.

> portion of the mediation effect I define to calculate was higher than 1,
> not mention the result of the new defined indirect effect a*b = 251.868.

Since this is based on unstandardized values, this seems non problematic.

Yves.
